audit.whatIsWrong: Rows 3, 4 and 6 disagreed with their own whys in both layers. Row 3 read Skill though whys[3] says 'he out-ranges and out-pokes me through the 4-5 stretch'; row 4 read Skill though whys[4] calls Slicing Maelstrom 'his single biggest window'; row 6 read Kennen though whys[6] opens 'Even again'.
audit.why: Kennen's Q reaches 950 and his W 725 against a 525 dash; there is no stage from 4 to 6 where Maokai holds the lane. Late, neither duels cleanly but Nature's Grasp is worth more in a 5v5.
audit.corrected: Row 3 -> Kennen, row 4 -> Kennen, row 6 -> Skill, as matched full+content pairs in one atomic group, matching both the packet chart and the mirror (kennen__maokai).

audit.whatIsWrong: Every stage was described as a Lightning Rush cooldown window, including Level 1 and the first-item stage. No real numbers anywhere.
audit.why: The actual spikes are his level-2 poke coming online, Slicing Maelstrom at 6 on a flat 120s, and his first AP item out-chipping Sap Magic. Lightning Rush (10/9/8/7/6s) is a repositioning tool, not the lane's clock.
audit.corrected: Real numbers written into phases[0..6].why, tldr, winCon, enemyWin, dosFull[0].d and breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: The decisive interaction was absent from the full layer entirely. Mark of the Storm stuns at three stacks, and Q, W and Lightning Rush each apply a stack — so his 'escape' is also his third mark. The page treated Lightning Rush purely as a get-out.
audit.why: Riot text: 'Kennen stuns enemies he hits 3 times with his abilities', and Lightning Rush explicitly applies a Mark of the Storm. That is why you count marks, not cooldowns, before stepping into a 525 W.
audit.corrected: Stated in report[5].t, winCon, dosFull[0].d, breakdown.cooldowns and phases[4].why.
sources: enemyKit P, Q, W, E text

edits.before: Passive heal + AA trades carry the early waves. Identify how Kennen contests the first waves before you commit anything.
edits.after: A wash at 1 — you have no combo and he only has Thundering Shuriken chip, so farm and let Sap Magic eat the poke.

edits.before: W root is your engage AND your peel — spend it once per fight. Only take the trade when Kennen's Lightning Rush is down.
edits.after: His 950-range Q out-ranges your 525 W by miles — you only get a trade when he oversteps into the wave to last-hit.

edits.before: Full kit online — your core pattern starts now. Keep the wave near your side so Kennen must walk into your engage range.
edits.after: Full poke kit plus energy costs mean he kites you between W cooldowns — you cannot fish for a dash you will miss.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Lightning Rush's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: He out-ranges you all through 4-5. Hold Sapling Toss on the wave to match his push, farm safe, and refuse the poke war you cannot win.

edits.before: Nature’s Grasp roots whole teams — lane it only for kill windows. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Kennen's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Slicing Maelstrom is 120s and stacks Mark of the Storm — three marks stun you out of any W. Never step up while his R is up.

edits.before: Heartsteel is your spike — force fights the moment it completes, on Lightning Rush's cooldown.
edits.after: His first AP item out-chips Sap Magic; your Bami line and E waveclear keep the lane stable.

edits.before: Two items on: your side-lane pattern is at full power. Kennen carry threat 7/10 — close before the map decides instead of you.
edits.after: Even late: you lose the duel, but Nature's Grasp walls his whole side in a 5v5. Carry threat 7/10 — fight where CC beats poke.

edits.before: Build MR — W-root him, out-sustain his poke. Maokai wins the Lightning Rush cooldown windows.
edits.after: Build MR and refuse the poke war — you only touch him when he oversteps into your 525 W range.

edits.before: Build MR and root him. Track Lightning Rush before every commit and keep the wave on your side.
edits.after: Build MR, hold W for his overstep, and never eat three Marks of the Storm; that stun is his all-in.

edits.before: Kennen wins by landing Lightning Rush, denying your pattern, and kiting you off the wave.
edits.after: Kennen wins by stacking three marks for the stun, then kiting your W cooldown from 950 range.

edits.before: His escape. Root before it. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Lightning Rush is 10-6s and adds a mark — count marks, not dashes.

edits.before: Track Kennen's Lightning Rush: His escape. Root before it. When it is down — W-Q + R him.
edits.after: Three Mark of the Storm procs stun you — his Q, W and E each apply one. Count to two.

edits.before: - Kennen Lightning Rush: matchup-defining — His escape. Root before it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Kennen Lightning Rush: matchup-defining — A 10-6s dash that also marks you. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.

notes:
Packet defect confirmed and NOT resolved by these edits: 'level chart contradicts data: Maokai wins 56.76% but the chart gives Kennen 5/7 stages vs 0'. My chart edits move it further that way (Kennen now takes 5 stages) because that is what the whys, the ranges and the mirror all say. The likely explanation is the sample — packet.games is 37 while the brief's top-level games is 155, so the 56.76% rides on 37 games. Flagged in questionsForUser rather than resolved by guessing.

The mirror agent's Sap Magic find is worth repeating from this side: the passive's cooldown drops each time Maokai is STRUCK BY a spell, so Kennen poking you actually accelerates your sustain. I did not write it into a lane string here because every candidate slot was already carrying a more decisive fact within the band, but it belongs in the itemization/anti-heal reasoning if a slot opens.

Champion-level kit-flag defect (third time this slice): Maokai's Q carries a 'grounding' flag Riot's description does not support. No grounding claim written — it would have been especially tempting here against Lightning Rush.
